history.summary: A modern replica of the Katra (Jammu) Vaishno Devi shrine, opened to devotees around 2007 by a private trust at Vaishnodevi Circle on the Sarkhej-Gandhinagar Highway. Rajasthani and Gujarati artisans built a ~50-ft artificial hillock of yellow sandstone simulating the Trikuta mountains; devotees crawl through narrow artificial caves to reach the sanctum, which houses the three stone pindis (Maha Kali, Maha Lakshmi, Maha Saraswati), with a small Bhairav Nath shrine completing the darshan loop. A large 1,350-sq-ft multi-level hall can hold thousands of pilgrims; Navratri is the peak festival. TOWN NOTE: the CSV town 'Ahmedabad' is kept but is imprecise — the temple sits on the city's northwestern outskirts near Khoraj, ~15-18 km from the city centre. TIMING CONFLICT (verify before visiting): sources report 5:30 AM-9:00 PM, 5:00 AM-10:00 PM, 6:00 AM-9:00 PM, and 6:00 AM-7:00 PM.

name: Vaishno Devi Temple, Ahmedabad
town_description: Ahmedabad is Gujarat's largest city and its former capital, founded in 1411 by Sultan Ahmed Shah I on the banks of the Sabarmati river. Its walled old city became India's first UNESCO World Heritage City in 2017, known for carved wooden havelis, pols, stepwells, and Sultanate-era monuments. Today it is a major industrial and commercial hub, famous for its food culture, the Sabarmati Ashram, and as the gateway to Gujarat.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri draws the largest crowds
